title: Multi-cluster SafeMode Guardrails for On‑Prem Upgrades
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact, operationally focused set of guardrails and playbook fragments for performing upgrades against multiple on‑prem / VPC private clusters. The goal is to minimize blast radius via a SafeMode strategy (automated degradations, scoped canaries, and fast rollback paths), and to call out concrete Terraform module practices, Helm/Argo rollout settings, and image attestation checkpoints so that CI/CD pipelines and oncall responders have predictable, testable steps.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments governed by the Private control plane (VPC & on‑prem package).
- Clusters are managed via GitOps (ArgoCD App-of-Apps pattern) and releases flow from a build pipeline into the gitops repo.
- Images are signed with cosign and SBOMs are produced.
- Terraform manages cluster networking, node pools and the platform operator installation; Helm manages Redwood platform charts.
- We assume working metrics and tracing exports into the observability stack (console dashboards exist per-cluster).

TL;DR (operationally actionable):
1) Block merge to production gitops repo unless: terraform plan OK, cosign attestation present, SBOM checksum matches, and smoke e2e passes in staging cluster.
2) Promote to 1–2 canary clusters (different failure domains) with Argo automated sync + controlled wave concurrency. Observe 15–30min signal window.
3) If regression signals tripped (latency spike, error rate > threshold, OOMs), flip SafeMode: auto-scale down traffic (traffic-splitting or circuit breaker) and trigger automated rollback to previously pinned image and helm release.
4) If rollback fails or signals persist, escalate to oncall SRE and promote cluster isolation (remove from LB pool), and open emergency rollout PR.

Key upgrade signals and thresholds (examples for automation):
- 5xx rate > 0.5% over baseline for 5m -> warn.
- p95 latency > baseline + 250ms for 10m -> warn.
- Token / cost anomalies (token consumption jump > 2x) -> warn.
- Memory RSS growth > 20% trend across pods in 3 successive 1m samples -> critical.
- CrashLoopBackOff count > 1 in primary canary -> critical.

Rollback matrix (short):
- Image-only regression (model binary or runtime): rollback image tag in helm values -> trigger Argo sync rollback.
- Helm values or chart change regression: revert chart PR in gitops repo -> Argo will reconcile.
- Node/kernel regression (OOM/driver bug): cordon affected nodes, scale up fallback pools, schedule node drainer job, and pin to previous machine image in terraform.
- Terraform infra drift causing control plane instability: freeze gitops sync, run terraform plan against state, and trigger infra rollback via operator documented steps.

Terraform module notes (practical pointers):
- Pin provider and module versions in module blocks and keep a migration schedule (see module-versioning.md in TF repo).
- Modules should expose explicit knobs: image_policy (allow_latest: bool), cosign_keyset_arn, node_pool_taints, kubelet_flags, and rolling_update_max_unavailable. These inputs allow ops to constrain upgrades without hand-editing modules.
- State safety: enable centralized remote state with state locking (S3+Dynamo or vault+consul), and require plan approvals via CI when changes touch: node_pool, k8s_version, or network.
- Plan validation step: add a custom terraform plan-check job that enforces a small diff on node counts and blocks changes to kubelet_flags unless an explicit flag is set.
- Drift remediation: export a ‘tf-diff-notifier’ artifact that posts human-friendly diffs to the release PR.

CI/CD pipeline pattern (build -> attest -> gitops PR):
1) Build image with reproducible tag (sha + short ref).
2) Run deterministic model integration smoke tests in ephemeral container.
3) Create SBOM (syft) and run vuln scan (grype). Block on critical CVEs.
4) Sign image and attestation with cosign. Publish attestation to OCI registry and push SBOM to artifacts bucket.
5) Create bot PR against gitops helm-values repo that updates image tag and cosign attestation digest, include the SBOM checksum. PR includes an autogenerated checklist (preflight results).
6) CI runs a dry-run Argo sync in staging cluster: apply manifest to staging via Argo's app-of-apps preview (no auto-sync in prod).
7) Auto-merge to prod gitops only after manual approval or automatic promotion policy (based on canary score).

Argo / Helm upgrade patterns and recommended settings:
- App-of-Apps: group releases by workload domain; each app has a separate sync policy.
- Sync options: use "Automated" with "Prune" for canary clusters only if you have a quick rollback hook. For prod clusters prefer "Manual" with a one-click promote.
- Hook-runner: use pre-sync hooks for node drain checks and post-sync hooks to trigger smoke endpoints. Keep hook timeouts conservative (2–5m).
- Helm chart practice: avoid pre/post-install logic that mutates cluster-wide resources. Keep charts idempotent and separate cluster-scoped resources into a distinct chart that is updated separately.
- Rolling upgrade constraints in values.yaml: set maxUnavailable small (10-20%) for critical services; for batch/worker services you can be more aggressive.
- Health checks: define rich readiness probes that include response shape checks (not just 200).

Image signing & attestation rules (enforcement checkpoints):
- CI must attach cosign attestation with SLSA provenance or equivalent for every image promoted to prod.
- The gitops promotion job validates cosign signature against the org keyring (store public keys in k8s secret via Sigstore integration or a KMS-backed secret for Private deployments).
- SBOM checksum must be present in the PR and validated by the post-merge job before Argo will auto-sync the cluster.

Preflight checks (scripts & examples):
- tf-plan-check.sh: run terraform plan and fail if change > configurable risk score.
- helm-values-lint: verify chart values schema plus policy checks (no allow_latest:true unless ephemeral).
- attestation-verify: cosign verify --keyset <org-keys.json> --type attestations <image> && check sbom checksum.
- smoke-e2e: curl /health + a small generation request; compare example payload checksum.

Canary orchestration recommendations:
- Canary groups: 3 stages (staging -> canary-1 -> canary-2 -> prod). Canary-1 should be in a different AZ/rack than canary-2 to catch infra‑specific regressions.
- Time windows: 15m observe window for quick regressions (crash loops, 5xx). 60m for performance regressions. These windows should be configurable per release.
- Automated score: use a simple weighted score over error rate (40%), p95 latency (30%), and resource anomalies (30%). Thresholds determine auto-promote or auto-rollback.

Emergency rollback runbook (short):
1) On critical signal, set Argo App of affected cluster to Manual sync and pause automated jobs.
2) Post a rollback comment to the release PR with "/rollback to <previous-tag>". Tag oncall SRE.
3) Trigger chart values revert PR and merge with expedited CI checks (skip nonblocking checks).
4) If merge fails, run Argo rollback CLI: argocd app rollback <app> <revision> --server <argocd-server> and watch events.
5) If rollback doesn’t stabilize, isolate cluster from east-west LB and route traffic to healthy cluster pool (DNS or LB weight change).
6) Collect artifacts: kubectl describe pod, kubelet logs, node dmesg, and controller-manager logs. Attach to incident page.

Observability and postmortem signals to collect:
- Argo events and sync history.
- Helm release history and chart diffs.
- Terraform change set and state change summary.
- Cosign attestation metadata and SBOM.
- Pod logs, OOM killer events, kernel messages.
- Latency and error traces correlated by trace id across services.

Open TODOs and follow-ups (practical):
- Add a Terraform knob to pause auto-upgrades of control plane components (owner: Liam).
- Build a lightweight promotion scorecard service that ingests metrics and outputs promote/rollback decisions (owner: Sofia).
- Create smoke endpoint contract and include it in platform SDKs (owner: Ethan).
- Document how to rotate cosign public keys in a Private deployment with KMS integration; provide a migration plan.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally prescriptive; the objective is to reduce human error during upgrades while keeping an escape hatch.
- Focus review on the Terraform inputs section and the image attestation handshake — these are the highest-risk automation points.

Appendix: quick checklist for a single upgrade push:
- [ ] Terraform plan run and approved for infra changes.
- [ ] Image built, SBOM generated, grype scan passed.
- [ ] Image signed and cosign attestation published.
- [ ] Bot PR created to gitops repo with tag + attestation + SBOM checksum.
- [ ] Staging sync successful and smoke-e2e green.
- [ ] Canary promotion engaged and observe window complete.
- [ ] Prod merge (manual or automated) and final monitor window.

Contact and escalation aliases:
- Oncall SRE: #sre-oncall (Slack), pager: SRE-Primary (PagerDuty)
- Platform lead: aisha.kumar@redwood.ai

End of doc (working draft).
